scores.evidence: CI authenticates to AWS and ECR through GitHub OIDC with per-repo role conditions. Remove every static credential.
scores.rationale: Mechanisms (OIDC, cosign keyless, Argo PreSync, expand/contract, pull-based GitOps) are used correctly; minor gaps like the Git-less emergency path versus Argo drift are not reconciled.

scores.evidence: Wave 1, about 10 services, chosen to cover every language, runtime and template path.
scores.rationale: Covers core needs with explicit deferrals, but lacks an upfront service inventory step beyond a Phase 0 check and defers contract testing.

scores.evidence: Git is the single record of what should run where, and changes are serialized through merges.
scores.rationale: Consistent GitOps design with clear ownership; small loose ends such as the emergency path bypassing Git while Argo self-heals.

scores.evidence: A release with an injected fault (5% 5xx) is aborted automatically within 10 min, with at most 5% of traffic exposed.
scores.rationale: Risky parts (rollback, fault injection, DR drill, game days, template contract tests) are validated early with checkable exits, though some thresholds like 15% and 5 min are unjustified.

scores.evidence: All 50 run as containers on Kubernetes (EKS)... This is an assumption to check in Phase 0.
scores.rationale: Key assumptions and revisit triggers are explicit, but team size, compliance, and build volume are not stated and some thresholds are arbitrary.

scores.evidence: Single-use runners (a compromised runner can't persist); ... game day: kill Argo CD mid-sync and simulate a Git-host outage
scores.rationale: Covers broken template blast radius, tampered artifacts, Git outage, failed migration and compromised runner; fork-PR secrets and flaky specifics are thin.

scores.evidence: Platform SLOs and error budget; ... platform disaster-recovery drill (restore Argo CD and registry in a second region
scores.rationale: Deploy, rollback, monitoring, DR and on-call routing via catalog are addressed, but platform team ownership and staffing are not named.

scores.evidence: Spot runners with retry, and a remote cache... Cost per pipeline run is tracked and trending flat or down.
scores.rationale: Runner cost controls and a buy-vs-build trigger exist, but there is no estimate from commit/build volume and cost work is deferred to Phase 5.

scores.evidence: Every service will copy this structure, so getting it wrong means 50 migrations later.
scores.rationale: Identifies one-way decisions (repo layout, artifact contract, template interface), validates them early on pilots, and gives revisit triggers and exit paths.

scores.evidence: A few off-the-shelf components connected by thin glue. The platform is not split into microservices.
scores.rationale: Adopts existing tools and defers heavy items, though Backstage, Kyverno and a full observability stack add some weight for an unspecified team.

scores.evidence: Within 15 minutes, `curl https://svc-pilot.prod.internal/version` returns the new commit SHA.
scores.rationale: Concrete first slice, dependency-justified phases, checkable exit criteria per phase, and revisit triggers for adapting.

checklist.evidence: Hand-build pipelines for 2 more services that differ deliberately from `svc-pilot`: another language
Old pipeline kept as fallback during overlap; wave pause at 15% change failure rate
Build once, promote the same image digest through dev → staging → prod.
CI authenticates to AWS and ECR through GitHub OIDC with per-repo role conditions. Remove every static credential.
Every image gets an SBOM (Syft) and SLSA provenance, and is signed with cosign using keyless signing.
Migrations follow expand/contract, run as an Argo PreSync job, and a failed migration stops the sync.
Cross-service contract testing (Pact). Pulled forward if breakage between services becomes the top cause of failed changes.
Flaky tests. Detect and quarantine them.
a build cache keyed on the lockfile hash.
Spot runners with retry, and a remote cache.
Platform SLOs and error budget: p95 CI queue time under 2 min

traps.evidence: Retire the old CI per service after 2 clean weeks, and revoke its credentials.
Images are addressed by digest only, never by a moving tag.
No secrets in Git or in CI variables.
Do not build a custom orchestrator.

note: Strong, well-sequenced GitOps plan with pilot-first waves and immutable digests; weaker on cost estimation, explicit fork-PR handling, flaky-test and contract-test depth, and team/ownership sizing.
